extraFacts.fact: A hose or tube size code is in sixteenths of an inch: 02 is 1/8 inch, 03 is 3/16 inch, 04 is 1/4 inch, 05 is 5/16 inch, 06 is 3/8 inch, 08 is 1/2 inch, 10 is 5/8 inch, 12 is 3/4 inch, 14 is 7/8 inch and 16 is 1 inch.
extraFacts.source: SAE J517 / SAE J1131 dash-size convention used across brass fitting makers

extraFacts.fact: Brass tube fittings, couplings and hose barbs are normally classified under HS subheading 7412.20 (copper-alloy tube or pipe fittings); the importer's customs broker has the final say.

ISO 7-1 covers pipe threads where the pressure-tight joint is made on the thread, such as the BSP taper (R) thread; ISO 228-1 covers pipe threads where the joint is not made on the thread, such as the BSP parallel (G) thread; ASME B1.20.1 is the general-purpose NPT pipe thread standard; ASME B1.20.3 covers Dryseal pipe threads, including NPTF; SAE J512 covers automotive tube fittings including flareless compression.
extraFacts.source: ISO 7-1, ISO 228-1, ASME B1.20.1, ASME B1.20.3, SAE J512

extraFacts.fact: SAE J2494 covers push-to-connect fittings for air brake tubing and FMVSS 571.106 covers brake hoses and their end fittings; the maker of the DOT push-in fittings states compliance with both. SAE J844 covers nonmetallic air brake tubing. DOT-approved air brake fittings are for compressed-air brake systems.

faqs.q: What is an aluminium sealing washer for BSP threads used for?
faqs.a: The Aluminium Sealing Washer for BSP Threads seals a BSP parallel-thread male stud against the face of the port, under the hex of the fitting. It is an aluminium washer in 4 sizes, from 1/8" to 1/2", and it is the seal that a parallel G thread needs, because that thread does not seal on its flanks.

faqs.q: How do I read the part number IH-BR-8400-06 on the aluminium BSP sealing washer?
faqs.a: The base number IH-BR-8400 is followed by one size code, in sixteenths of an inch: 06 is 3/8" BSPP (G3/8-19). The same rule holds on every row, so IH-BR-8400-02 is 1/8" BSPP (G1/8-28), IH-BR-8400-04 is 1/4" and IH-BR-8400-08 is 1/2" (G1/2-14).

faqs.q: Which sizes does the aluminium sealing washer for BSP threads come in?
faqs.a: The washer comes in 4 part numbers, one for each of 1/8" (IH-BR-8400-02), 1/4" (IH-BR-8400-04), 3/8" (IH-BR-8400-06) and 1/2" (IH-BR-8400-08) BSPP. Larger washers are quoted on request; send the thread size of the stud.

faqs.q: How do I pick the right BSP sealing washer for a male stud?
faqs.a: Read the thread size on the stud, for example G3/8-19, and choose the row with the same size: IH-BR-8400-06 for G3/8-19. The washer sits under the hex of the stud, so its inside diameter must clear the thread and its outside diameter must fit the port face.

faqs.q: What pressure can an aluminium BSP sealing washer hold?
faqs.a: The manufacturer publishes no pressure rating for the washer, because the joint rating belongs to the fitting and port. Tell us the medium, working pressure and temperature and we confirm the washer before you order the Aluminium Sealing Washer for BSP Threads.

faqs.q: Why is the BSP sealing washer made of aluminium?
faqs.a: The listing gives the material as aluminium. A soft aluminium washer crushes slightly between the stud hex and the port face to seal, and it is replaced each time the joint is remade. Tell us the fluid if aluminium could be a problem.

faqs.q: Which standard applies to the aluminium washer for BSP threads?
faqs.a: The listing names ISO 228-1, which covers pipe threads where the joint is not made on the thread, such as the BSP parallel (G) thread. The washer is the seal for that kind of thread. Ask us for any other document you need and we ask the maker.

faqs.q: Which fittings use the aluminium sealing washer for BSP threads?
faqs.a: Any BSP parallel-thread male stud that seals on the port face, such as a BSPP male adapter. See the [brass BSPP male × BSPP male adapter](/p/brass-bspp-male-x-bspp-male-adapter) and the [brass BSP and metric adapters shelf](/c/brass-bsp-metric-adapters); the washer is not for taper (BSPT) threads, which seal on the thread.

faqs.q: How should an aluminium BSP sealing washer be fitted?
faqs.a: Fit a new washer under the hex of the BSPP male stud every time the joint is made, seat it flat on the port face and tighten until the washer is crushed evenly. Do not reuse a flattened washer; our [guide to brass pipe fittings, NPTF and BSP](/blog/brass-pipe-fittings-nptf-and-bsp) explains parallel and taper BSP threads.
